critical_point: Floor division rounds down, so -7 // 2 is -4, and quotient times divisor plus remainder gives the dividend back.
stem: Read the program below, then choose exactly what it prints when it runs from the first line to the last.
reason: 7 // -2 rounds down to -4, and the remainder is 7 - (-2 * -4) = -1; quotient times divisor plus remainder gives 7 back.
question: Q1
tip: Division with // rounds down, not toward zero; check with quotient times divisor plus remainder.

critical_point: Assigning a list to another name copies the reference and never the list, so both names reach one list.
stem: After this program runs, which statement correctly says what it prints and why the two lengths differ?
options_or_blanks: 3 3: append works on a private copy, so no list changes
4 4: the copy keeps a link, so c grows along with a
4 3: b is a second name for the list of a, but c was copied
3 4: b got its own list and c shares the list of a
reason: b = a adds a second name for one list, so append through b changes a; a[:] builds a new list that stays at 3 items.

tip: A name is a tag on a list; assigning one name to another adds a tag, not a list.

critical_point: Errors of the user are raised; errors of the programmer are asserted.
stem: An assert is meant for mistakes of the [[1]]. Because Python can [[2]] every assert when started in optimised mode, an assert must never be the only [[3]] against bad user input.
reason: Errors of the user are raised, errors of the programmer are asserted; python -O removes every assert, so it cannot be the only guard.

critical_point: enumerate and zip replace index arithmetic such as range(len(names)).
stem: Match each situation to the tool that fits it best. Two of the seven tools fit none of the situations.

premises: Print every item of a shopping list together with its number, counting from 1
Combine a list of names with a list of scores, one pair at a time
Keep asking until the player types the right password
Find the price of a product quickly from its name
Save the stock table in a text form that other programs can also read
answers: A while loop that tests each answer
A recursive function with no base case
enumerate with a start value of 1
A mapping from each product name to its price
A global variable shared by all functions
Text in JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) made with json.dumps

reason: enumerate(items, 1) numbers from 1; zip pairs two lists; while repeats until the test fails; a mapping finds a value by key; json.dumps writes a dictionary as text.
question: Q3
tip: enumerate gives each item with a counter; zip walks several lists side by side.

critical_point: A dictionary key must be hashable, so a tuple can be a key and a list is refused with a TypeError.
stem: A programmer wants the pair (2, 3) as a key in a dictionary, but a list [2, 3] is refused. Which reason explains this?
options_or_blanks: A list is too long to be stored, while a pair always fits
Keys must be numbers, and a list is not a number
A list may change later, so its fingerprint could change and the stored pair would be lost
A list cannot be compared, so no key can ever be found
reason: A key must be hashable: its fingerprint must never change, so a pair is accepted and a list is refused with a TypeError.
question: Q3
tip: A dictionary stores values under keys and finds each one again from a fingerprint of the key.

critical_point: Calling spam.upper() leaves spam unchanged until the result is assigned back.
stem: A learner writes name.upper() alone on one line and name stays the same, yet team.sort() changes team. What best explains the difference?
options_or_blanks: A string cannot be changed in place, so upper() builds a new string, while a list can be changed in place
upper() works only inside print, while sort() works anywhere in the program
Strings are copied at every use, while lists are never copied by Python
upper() is a slow method, so Python delays its effect until the program ends
reason: Strings never change, so upper() returns a new string that must be kept; sort() changes the list itself and returns None.
